Subject: PII handling for prompts/outputs \u2014 follow-up and next steps

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to hear more about BrightPath's use case for summarization and triage. As promised, summary of how Redwood handles prompts and outputs and proposed next steps so your security team can validate: 

Summary (hosted API):
- Storage: Raw prompts and generated outputs are retained by default for 7 days for debugging and abuse monitoring, then purged. We do not use prompts/outputs to train or improve public models.
- Logging: Short-term request logs (metadata: request id, model variant, latency, truncated token counts) are kept for 30 days for observability. Full request/response payloads are treated as described above.
- Redaction: Customers can configure client-side redaction before sending PII. We offer SDK helpers and a redaction checklist.
- Residency & encryption: Data is stored in the region you select (US or EU) and is encrypted at rest with AES-256. Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) are available on Dedicated/Private plans.
- Access & audit: All access to stored request payloads is logged in audit trails. We offer role-based access controls and can forward audit logs to your SIEM.
- Alternatives: For no retention, we can run on Dedicated or Private where you can disable host-side logging and keep all logs inside your VPC.

Attachments: I attached a short PDF summarizing the above plus our DPA highlights (redwood-pii-handling-summary.pdf, redwood-dpa-datasheet.pdf).

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm which of the following BrightPath will send to Redwood in production? (a) full patient notes with PHI, (b) de-identified text, (c) tokenized ids only
2) Would your security team prefer a live review (30-45 min) where we walk through retention, KMS, and audit logs?
3) If residency is required in EU for any subset of traffic, please flag that now so we can provide region-specific configs.

I can join a call with your security lead next week — Tue/Wed/Thu AM PST works for me.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0173

Thanks Rishi — really helpful summary. A few clarifying questions before I loop in our security/compliance folks:

1) When you say prompts/outputs are retained 7 days by default, is that the full unredacted text or are there automatic redaction policies applied on the server side?
2) Are logs (even metadata) ever replicated outside the selected region (for example to a central analytics cluster)?
3) For audit purposes we need to prove that prompts/outputs were not used to train models. Do you have a statement/policy we can include in our SOC / vendor questionnaire?
4) Can you confirm whether the 7-day retention applies to streaming tokens in streaming calls (we sometimes stream incrementally)?

We will most likely send PHI in early testing (de-identified where possible) but need to understand the options for zero retention so we can plan the PoC. Also can you send your DPA and SOC 2 report link?

Best,

Sofia — thanks for the great questions. Answers below (TL;DR included at top).

TL;DR: Hosted API default retains full request/response payloads for 7 days (unredacted) for debugging/abuse monitoring; streaming tokens follow same retention behavior. We do not use customer prompts/outputs to train models and can provide a signed statement. For zero retention or customer-managed keys, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments.

Detailed answers:
1) Server-side redaction: No automatic redaction is performed by default — we retain the full payloads for the seven-day window. We provide SDK helpers and best-practice guides to help clients redact PII before sending. If you require host-side redaction rules we can discuss a configuration for Dedicated deployments, but default hosted plan expects client-side redaction.

2) Log replication / region: Request payloads and logs are stored only in the region you select (US or EU). Aggregated metrics may be sent to a central telemetry pipeline for operational metrics, but that telemetry contains only non-identifying metadata (latency, error codes, model id). Full payloads are not replicated across regions.

3) Training statement: Redwood has a clear policy that customer prompts and outputs are not used to train our public models. I attached a one-page vendor statement and our DPA excerpt (see attached PDF). We can also provide a signed attestation for SOC reviews.

4) Streaming retention: Streaming sessions are reconstructed and stored as full request/response payloads. The 7-day retention applies to the reconstructed payload for debugging purposes.

Options to meet zero/short retention requirements:
- Dedicated: Reserved GPU pools where you can disable host-side payload retention; customer logs can be forwarded to your SIEM or stored in your VPC.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): No Redwood-hosted payloads; everything stays inside your network and under your KMS.
- Host-side truncation: For POCs, we can configure a per-account policy to keep only metadata and truncate payloads after 24 hours while we complete the security review (subject to change based on product team approval).

Next steps I'd propose:
- I can share our SOC 2 Type II report and the standard DPA via a secure link (I'll drop the links).
- Schedule a 30-45 minute technical review with Marissa (Customer Engineering) and our security engineer to walk through KMS, audit logs, and deployment options.

Availability: Tue/Thu 9-11am PST this week for a quick call.

Regards,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
